# Operator Overloading
<!-- Slide 10 -->

## How Can a Class Define Its Own Arithmetic?

- C++ already gives arithmetic operators familiar meanings for built-in values.
- An operator method lets a class define what those symbols mean for its objects.

::: notes
Slides 10–15
:::

<!-- Slide 11 -->

---

## The `operator+` Method

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
<div style="font-size:50%">

~~~cpp
// overloadPlus.cpp
#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

class Point2D {
private:
    int x;
    int y;

public:
    Point2D(int xValue = 0, int yValue = 0);
    Point2D operator+(const Point2D& other) const;
    void print() const;
};

Point2D::Point2D(int xValue, int yValue) {
    x = xValue;
    y = yValue;
}

Point2D Point2D::operator+(const Point2D& other) const {
    return Point2D(x + other.x, y + other.y);
}

void Point2D::print() const {
    cout << "(" << x << ", " << y << ")" << endl;
}

int main() {
    Point2D first(2, 3);
    Point2D second(4, 1);
    Point2D total = first + second;

    total.print();

    return 0;
}
~~~

</div>
:::
::: {.column width="40%"}
**Output**

~~~text
(6, 4)
~~~
:::
:::

::: notes
Source file: cpp/overloadPlus.cpp
:::

## The `operator-` Method

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
<div style="font-size:50%">

~~~cpp
// overloadminus.cpp
#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

class Point2D {
private:
    int x;
    int y;

public:
    Point2D(int xValue = 0, int yValue = 0);
    Point2D operator-(const Point2D& other) const;
    void print() const;
};

Point2D::Point2D(int xValue, int yValue) {
    x = xValue;
    y = yValue;
}

Point2D Point2D::operator-(const Point2D& other) const {
    return Point2D(x - other.x, y - other.y);
}

void Point2D::print() const {
    cout << "(" << x << ", " << y << ")" << endl;
}

int main() {
    Point2D first(8, 5);
    Point2D second(3, 7);
    Point2D difference = first - second;

    difference.print();

    return 0;
}
~~~

</div>
:::
::: {.column width="40%"}
**Output**

~~~text
(5, -2)
~~~
:::
:::

::: notes
Source file: cpp/overloadminus.cpp
:::

## Prefix and Postfix `operator++`

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
<div style="font-size:50%">

~~~cpp
// demoPrePost.cpp
#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

class Counter {
private:
    int value;

public:
    Counter(int start = 0);
    Counter& operator++();
    Counter operator++(int);
    void print() const;
};

Counter::Counter(int start) {
    value = start;
}

Counter& Counter::operator++() {
    ++value;
    return *this;
}

Counter Counter::operator++(int) {
    Counter original = *this;
    ++value;
    return original;
}

void Counter::print() const {
    cout << value << endl;
}

int main() {
    Counter count(5);
    Counter prefixResult = ++count;
    prefixResult.print();
    count.print();

    Counter postfixResult = count++;
    postfixResult.print();
    count.print();

    return 0;
}
~~~

</div>
:::
::: {.column width="40%"}
**Output**

~~~text
6
6
6
7
~~~
:::
:::

::: notes
Source file: cpp/demoPrePost.cpp
:::

<!-- Slide 14 -->

---

## Operator Methods Combine Object State

- `operator+` and `operator-` return new objects built from two operands.
- Prefix `operator++` changes the object before returning it. Postfix `operator++` returns the original value before changing the object.
